subtitle: Poets, Ports and the Rival Crowns of Tamilakam

panels.shot: vast aerial view over the Indian peninsula, camera drifting south to a lush, river-cut Tamilakam
panels.action: The southern tip of the subcontinent stretches under monsoon clouds, rivers like silver threads meeting the sea along a dark green Tamil coast.

dialogue.text: In the age of Ashoka’s distant roar, Tamilakam lay beyond Mauryan spears—a land of three crowns, hill chiefs, poets and restless roads.

i18n.hi: अशोक की दूर की गूँज के समय, तमिलकम मौर्य भालों से परे था—तीन मुकुट, पहाड़ी सरदार, कवि और बेचैन राहों की धरती।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a rock-cut Ashokan edict in a lonely landscape
panels.action: An ancient rock face dominates the frame, its surface carved with Ashokan Prakrit lines, the land around silent and empty under a pale sky.

dialogue.text: On distant rocks, Ashoka carved names—Choda, Pandya, Keralaputra, Satiyaputra—realms he did not rule, yet sought to touch with his dhamma.

i18n.hi: दूर चट्टानों पर अशोक ने नाम उकेरे—चोडा, पांड्य, केरलपुत्र, सतीयपुत्र—राज्य जिन्हें वो नहीं चलाता था, पर धम्म से छूना चाहता था।

panels.shot: sweeping map-style bird’s-eye, focusing on Tamilakam with highlighted regions
panels.action: A stylized parchment map shows Tamilakam: western hills and coast, central Kaveri plains, eastern seaboard and deep southern interior, each region glowing faintly.

dialogue.text: Tamilakam was many lands—western Chera country, Chola river plains, Pandya hills and ports, and Velir-chief territories threading between them.

i18n.hi: तमिलकम कई भूभाग था—पश्चिम का चे‍रा देश, चोला की नदी घाटियाँ, पांड्य की पहाड़ियाँ और बंदरगाह, और इनके बीच फैली वेलिर सरदारियों।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Karur-like Chera interior, hills and trade path
panels.action: A winding track climbs through low forested hills toward a settlement of wooden halls and earth ramparts, pack animals and traders moving like ants along the path.

dialogue.text: In the west, Chera lords guarded hill roads and river valleys, watching caravans from the north and ships from the Erythraean Sea.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम में चे‍रा नरेश पहाड़ी रास्तों और नदी घाटियों की रखवाली करते, उत्तर से आती करवानों और एरिथ्रियन सागर से उठते जहाज़ों पर नज़र रखते।

panels.shot: regal mid-shot of Karikala Chola seated in Urayur, symbolic of Chola power
panels.action: Karikala Chola sits on a simple yet high throne in a timber hall at Urayur, his posture alert, tiger-bannered spears flanking him as courtiers stand in shadow.

dialogue.text: To the east, Chola rulers in Urayur and Kaveripattinam held the Kaveri plains, their tiger emblem marking rice fields, river fords and coastal harbours.

i18n.hi: पूरब में उरैयूर और कावेरीपट्टनम के चोला शासक कावेरी के मैदान थामे थे, उनका बाघ चिन्ह धान के खेत, नदी घाट और समुद्री बंदरगाहों पर दिखता था।

panels.shot: sunset wide shot of Madurai’s early fort and streets
panels.action: Early Madurai spreads around a fortified mound, thatched houses and market stalls packed tight, palm trees and temple towers just emerging against a red sky.

dialogue.text: Further south, Pandya kings of Madurai ruled from walled towns and pearl shores, their fish symbol known from inland cattle pens to sea-facing wharves.

i18n.hi: और दक्षिण में मदुरै के पांड्य राजा किलेबंद नगरों और मोती किनारों से राज करते, उनकी मछली की मुहर भीतर के गोशालों से लेकर समुद्री घाटों तक पहचान थी।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of a Sangam assembly with poets and patrons
panels.action: In a pillared hall lit by oil lamps, kings and chiefs sit on mats as aged and youthful poets recite, a palm-leaf manuscript resting by a bronze lamp.

dialogue.text: Their world lives in Sangam songs—poems of war and wisdom where Chera bows, Chola tigers and Pandya fish share space with hungry bards and proud mothers.

i18n.hi: उनकी दुनिया संगम गीतों में बसती है—युद्ध और बुद्धि के पद जहाँ चे‍रा के धनुष, चोला के बाघ और पांड्य की मछली भूखे कवियों और गर्वीली माताओं के संग चलते हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide of Venni, Karikala as a central figure in the chaos
panels.action: On the plain of Venni, Karikala Chola stands in the midst of chariots and infantry poised to clash, banners whipping in the wind as rival standards face him across trampled earth.

dialogue.text: One poem recalls Venni, where Karikala broke a confederacy of foes, his victory turning the Kaveri country into Chola ground for a generation.

i18n.hi: एक कविता वेन्नि की याद करती है, जहाँ करिकाल ने दुश्मन संघ को तोड़ दिया, उसकी जीत ने एक पीढ़ी को कावेरी देश को चोला ज़मीन बना डाला।

panels.shot: tight mid-shot in a royal camp, Karikala listening to a poet
panels.action: Karikala sits beneath a war tent awning, armour stacked behind him, as a lean poet stands before him, palm-leaf raised, eyes bright with the thrill of recitation.

dialogue.speaker: the_chera_chola_and_pandya_houses
dialogue.text: Sing not of my might alone—tell of those who fell and those who fed them.

i18n.hi: केवल मेरी ताकत मत गाओ—उनका भी गाओ जो गिरे, और जो उन्हें खिलाते रहे।

panels.shot: moody mid-shot of a village after a cattle raid, smoke and silence
panels.action: A Tamil village lies quiet after a raid; cattle pens stand empty, a few elders and women watch the dusty track, cooking fires smouldering under a grey dawn.

dialogue.text: Sangam war is not only kings. Poems dwell on cattle raids, burning hamlets, the ache of widows, and the lean years after honor was won.

i18n.hi: संगम का युद्ध सिर्फ राजाओं का नहीं। कविताएँ मवेशी लूट, जलती बस्तियों, विधवाओं की टीस और उस दुबले समय पर ठहरती हैं जब मान तो मिला, पेट खाली रहा।

panels.shot: close-up of a mother’s face hearing news of her son, inspired by Purananuru themes
panels.action: An older woman sits at a doorway, her face hard yet wet-eyed, fingers clutching her upper cloth as a messenger stands before her, speechless.

dialogue.text: In Purananuru, mothers speak with iron tongues, praising sons who die well yet cursing rulers when war forgets justice and care for the poor.

i18n.hi: पुरनानूरु में माँएँ लोहे-सी ज़ुबान से बोलती हैं—अच्छी मौत मरने वाले बेटों की सराह करते हुए भी राजाओं को कोसती हैं जब युद्ध न्याय और गरीबों की देखभाल भूल जाता है।

panels.shot: busy wide shot of Kaveripattinam harbour, ships and foreign traders
panels.action: At Kaveripattinam’s harbour, wooden ships crowd the water, foreign merchants in varied dress haggle with Tamil traders as mounds of pepper and textiles lie piled on the quay.

dialogue.text: Ports like Kaveripattinam and Muziris tied the crowns to the wider sea, where Roman, West Asian and northern Indian traders sought pearls, spices and fine cloth.

i18n.hi: कावेरीपट्टनम और मुज़िरिस जैसे बंदरगाह मुकुटों को बड़े समंदर से जोड़ते थे, जहाँ रोमी, पश्चिम एशियाई और उत्तर भारत के व्यापारी मोती, मसाले और बढ़िया कपड़े खोजते थे।

panels.shot: archaeological close-up of a Tamil Brahmi potsherd and coins
panels.action: On a wooden table, a Tamil Brahmi-inscribed potsherd lies beside punch-marked coins and rouletted ware, lit by a slanting beam as if freshly unearthed.

dialogue.text: Tamil Brahmi on pots and stones, coins and imported wares now anchor the poems—proof that bards sang of a world thick with trade routes and written marks.

i18n.hi: मिट्टी के बर्तनों, पत्थरों, सिक्कों और आयातित सामान पर तमिल ब्राह्मी अब इन गीतों को थामती है—सबूत कि कवि उस दुनिया को गा रहे थे जहाँ राहें और लिखे निशान घने थे।

panels.shot: distant view of hills and a bannered camp, evoking Kharavela’s Hathigumpha horizon
panels.action: Beyond a rocky ridge, a small bannered camp stands near a pass, hills stretching toward the south under a hazy sky, giving a sense of unseen confederacies.

dialogue.text: Far off, Kharavela’s Hathigumpha record hints at a Tamil confederacy—fleeting words on stone showing that these polities were known, not bound, by northern kings.

i18n.hi: दूर खड़वेल की हाथीगुम्फा लेख तमिल संघ की आहट देता है—पत्थर पर थोड़े से शब्द दिखाते हैं कि ये राज्य उत्तर के राजाओं को मालूम थे, पर उनकी ज़ंजीर में नहीं बँधे थे।

panels.shot: symbolic triptych-style wide shot: bow, tiger, fish standards facing but not merging
panels.action: Three tall standards stand apart on an open plain: a handsome bow, a fierce tiger and a twin fish, their cloth stirring in the wind yet each planted in separate soil.

dialogue.text: The Chera bow, Chola tiger and Pandya fish shared tongue, gods and bards, but never fused into one realm; alliance and rivalry rose and fell like monsoon clouds.

i18n.hi: चे‍रा का धनुष, चोला का बाघ और पांड्य की मछली भाषा, देवताओं और कवियों में साझी थे, पर एक साम्राज्य में नहीं घुले; मेल-मिलाप और टकराव मानसून बादलों की तरह उठते-गिरते रहे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a poet writing on palm leaf by lamplight
panels.action: A lone poet bends over a palm leaf, stylus poised, oil lamp flickering beside him as night presses at the doorway, his face intent and weary.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars read Champakalakshmi, Mahadevan and the old songs together, seeing in them a mosaic of chiefdoms, markets and courts rather than neat kingdoms.

i18n.hi: आज के विद्वान चम्पकलक्ष्मी, महादेवन और पुराने गीतों को साथ पढ़ते हैं, उनमें सुव्यवस्थित राज्यों से ज़्यादा सरदारियों, बाज़ारों और दरबारों की रंगीन चितरावट देखते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle mid-shot of Karikala on a riverbank, looking over fields and roads
panels.action: Karikala stands on a Kaveri bank at dusk, watching farmers, merchants and soldiers move along the water’s edge, his tiger banner dim against the soft light.

dialogue.text: Rulers like Karikala lived in a web of shared culture, where keeping roads open, poets fed, and honor balanced mattered as much as holding land.

i18n.hi: करिकाल जैसे शासक साझा संस्कृति के जाल में जीते थे, जहाँ राहें खुली रखना, कवियों को खिलाना और मान की तराज़ू सँभालना ज़मीन पकड़ने जितना ज़रूरी था।

panels.shot: broad closing wide of Tamilakam’s landscapes—hills, fields, ports—under one sky
panels.action: Hills, paddy fields, cattle herds and bustling ports stretch in one panoramic sweep under a single vast sky, dotted in the distance with faint symbols of bow, tiger and fish.

dialogue.text: The realm of the three crowns endures in stone and song, reminding us that a people may share language and memory without needing a single king to bind them.

i18n.hi: तीन मुकुटों की यह दुनिया पत्थर और गीतों में ज़िंदा है, याद दिलाते हुए कि लोग भाषा और यादें बाँट सकते हैं—बिना किसी एक राजा की डोरी के भी।

title_i18n.en: The Realm of the Three Crowns

subtitle_i18n.en: Poets, Ports and the Rival Crowns of Tamilakam
subtitle_i18n.hi: कवि, बंदरगाह और तमिलकम की टकराती ताजियाँ
